what: #1258 (Tier 1, F3-02 and F3-04): `regrain()`, `regrain_history()` and a hand `regrain_step` do not refuse a REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE caller (transmute, untransmute and from_hypertable do, through `_refuse_strict_isolation`), so the copy reads the source through the caller's old snapshot and the swap drops a row another session committed after it (F3-02: {10,20} instead of {10,20,500}); under a hand swap tick in a REPEATABLE READ transaction, or a database default_transaction_isolation that maintain inherits, the residual reconcile loop and `_regrain_delta_count` after the DETACH read the delta through the tick's first snapshot, so a writer's committed UPDATE made while the swap waited is reverted (F3-04: row 10 ends `orig`). docs/reference.md even contemplates "a REPEATABLE READ caller of regrain" without a refusal. Fix shape: `_refuse_strict_isolation` at every regrain entry point (`regrain()`, `regrain_history()`, `regrain_step()`, and `maintain`'s swap path, which under a stricter database default must refuse or run the tick's reads as of a fresh snapshot), with the remedy in the message, and the reference saying so; say which entry points the fix covers. Acceptance: F3-02's `repro.sql` and F3-04's `repro.sh`.

#1259 (Tier 1, F14-01, rebuilt by its verifier): `_part_built`, `_part_detached_by_hand` and `_archive_hold_partition` vouch for a `retiring_at` mark by itself, without the dispatch record (`pgpm.part.detach_dispatched_oid`) that #1250 taught `retire()`, `_detach_reap`, `_retain_recall` and the install's pass to require. A partition whose `retire()` stamped the mark but whose dispatch failed (no pg_cron), then detached by hand by the operator, is handed to the archive strategy by the next `maintain()` tick (the archive step runs before `retain()`) and recorded as covered with no rows; when the operator attaches it back, the remedy the reference's retire entry gives, retention drops it on that false coverage and rows 1, 2 and 15 are in neither the table nor the archive. Fix shape: one rule for "is this mark pgpm's own" shared by every reader of `retiring_at` (the three named here and any other: grep `retiring_at` in the core and the modules), the mark vouching only with `detach_dispatched_oid`, so an unvouched mark reads as the operator's at every site; say which sites the fix covers. Acceptance: F14-01's `repro.verified.sql`.

#1260 (Tier 1, F5-02): `archive._owned_key` claims key bases as raw TEXT, `p_prefix` exactly as `archive.configure` stored it, while MinIO (the store the harness and pgpm_archive/README.md name) resolves '/P/x' and 'P/x' to one object. A table that takes a dropped table's name, configured with the same prefix spelled with a leading slash, claims the unclaimed base '/P/public.t', keeps the PLAIN key shape, and its chunk PUT replaces the dropped table's object, the only copy of the rows retire() dropped; the reference promises a later namesake gets the oid-shaped key and cannot overwrite. Fix shape: canonicalise the prefix where it is stored and where keys are claimed (no leading slash, no '//' , no '..'; refuse what cannot be canonicalised, naming it) so one object has one claim whatever the spelling, and say whether other stores (AWS keeps the two keys distinct) change the contract; docs. Acceptance: F5-02's `repro.sql` (archive harness: fixtures first).

#1261 (Tier 2, F3-03): `_regrain_copy_make` builds each copy `LIKE <parent> INCLUDING CONSTRAINTS`, which gives the copy every CHECK of the parent as a VALIDATED one, a NOT VALID CHECK included; a row written before the CHECK, which the table still serves, fails every copy batch with 23514, so `regrain()` and `regrain_history()` raise and auto-regrain logs `skip_regrain` on every tick with the capture and the TRUNCATE refusal left on the monolith until `regrain_cancel`. #633's fix leaves NOT VALID foreign keys off the copy for exactly this reason and left CHECKs. Fix shape: carry a parent's NOT VALID CHECK onto the copy as NOT VALID (or leave it off and let the swap's ATTACH adopt the parent's), so a row the parent serves is copied; the same for the hypertable copy if it shares the LIKE (say). Acceptance: F3-03's `repro.sql`.

#1262 (Tier 3, F4-03 and F11-03): `adopt_partition` judges "attached, not pending" from `pg_inherits` through the caller's transaction snapshot, both before and after its SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, and documents no isolation requirement, so a REPEATABLE READ caller whose snapshot predates another session's committed DETACH records the detached table in `pgpm.part` as attached (the READ COMMITTED call on the same state refuses), against the function's header ("the relation judged attached is still attached when its row commits") and the reference. Fix shape: `_refuse_strict_isolation` up front (the transmute shape) and the re-read under the lock made as of the lock (`pg_partition_ancestors` the way `retire()` reads it, or a fresh snapshot), say which. Acceptance: F4-03's `repro.sql` and F11-03's `repro.sql`.

#1263 (Tier 3, F13-01): `_snapshot_wait` judges "this session cannot see the copies" by `backend_xmin`, which is the cluster-wide oldest running xid: a transaction older than `regrain_written_xid` open in ANOTHER database holds back the xmin of every statement in this one, so the swap defers at its budget for that transaction's whole life and the refusal names an innocent local pid, against docs/reference.md ("the wait ends once no session holds a snapshot that could miss a copy"; "other databases ... are not consulted"). The wait is the lever phase's #1253 (ten verification rounds; read its comments and tests/328 before touching it). Fix shape: judge a local session by what its snapshot can see rather than by the cluster-wide floor where PostgreSQL lets you (a session whose backend_xmin is held back only by a transaction of another database has a snapshot that can see the copies; the oldest xid among THIS database's running transactions is the floor that matters), keeping every rule tests/328 pins; where the catalog cannot tell the two apart, say so and make the message name the holding transaction's database instead of the local pid; docs. Acceptance: F13-01's `repro.sh` (two databases in one container).

#1264 (Tier 3, F15-02, rebuilt by its verifier): `_over_retired_chunks` casts a legacy offset-less retired ledger `hi` (a pre-#977 strategy's covered_hi stored verbatim; no upgrade normalises those rows) in the caller's session TimeZone, so the same call holds the first partition from a UTC session and nothing from Asia/Kolkata, against tests/317's contract (the same answer from any session zone). Fix shape: read an offset-less bound as the grid's own instant (`partition_tz`, or UTC as the ledger's canonical text promises), the way `_native_order_key` and the #500 rule read stored text, and consider an upgrade pass that canonicalises those rows once; say which. Acceptance: F15-02's `repro.verified.sql`.

#1265 (Tier 3, F2-02): `check_time_monotonic` compares a naive `timestamp` column cast to timestamptz in the caller's session TimeZone, so a column that rises with the id (01:50, 02:30, 03:15 on 2026-03-08) reports 1.0 from a UTC session and 0.5 from America/New_York, because 02:30 falls in the spring-forward gap; the reference defines the result as the fraction of adjacent pairs whose time is non-decreasing and says nothing about the session zone. Fix shape: compare a naive column as itself (or in UTC), never through the session zone, and the same at any sibling check function (`check_uuidv7`, `check_text_time`) that casts a naive column. Acceptance: F2-02's `repro.sql`.

#1266 (Tier 3, F6-02): `from_hypertable_copy` resolves the key's constraint name with `select conname ... where conindid = v_keyidx` and no `conrelid`/`contype` filter; an incoming foreign key that references the hypertable's primary key (allowed in TimescaleDB 2.16) shares that conindid, and when its catalog row comes first the copy pre-builds `<fk>_pgpm_new` and the cutover builds the key a second time, leaving a stray redundant UNIQUE index on the migrated table, against the reference's promise that the copy's key index is adopted rather than rebuilt. Fix shape: resolve the constraint by `conrelid = hypertable and contype in ('p','u') and conindid = ...`, and the same wherever the module or core resolves a constraint by index alone (grep `conindid`). Acceptance: F6-02's `repro.sql` (timescale harness; the catalog order is forced by RENAME CONSTRAINT).

#1267 (Tier 3, F6-03): `_surface_prepare` drops a surface function whose shape changed (a pre-#343 `status()` without `regrain_to`) and recreates it, and `_surface_unreplaceable` looks only at pg_depend dependants, never at the function's grants, so an upgrade silently undoes the operator's `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC` and `GRANT EXECUTE` to a monitoring role, against the install's #983 header, which promises the upgrade keeps the function's grants or refuses. Fix shape: record the ACL before the drop and reapply it after the create (the `_acl_carry_ddl` shape), or refuse naming the grants; the same for every surface function the helper drops. Acceptance: F6-03's `repro.sh`.

part_of: Addresses #1232 (the remedy of _time_unit_contract's date-anchor and timestamp(p) refusals when raised through from_hypertable)
what: #1268 (Tier 3, F16r-01): `_from_hypertable_check_arguments` asks transmute's sign rules and `_time_unit_contract` before the copy and the swap but not transmute's "mixed month + duration interval unsupported" rule (raised in `_grid_floor`), so with `p_interval '1 mon 1 day'` both `from_hypertable` and `from_hypertable_cutover` copy and commit the swap, the hypertable and its incoming foreign key are gone, and only then does transmute refuse, leaving a plain unregistered table (the #1085 shape for a fourth argument rule; the reference says transmute's argument rules are asked first). #1232 (open, Tier 4, re-found as F16-01): the date-anchor and timestamp(p) refusals `_time_unit_contract` raises through `from_hypertable` carry transmute's remedy ("re-run transmute ... call pgpm.transmute_abort first"), which does not apply to a hypertable; nothing from_hypertable did leaves a bound for transmute_abort. Fix shape: ask the mixed-interval rule (and every other rule `_grid_floor` or transmute's preflight would raise for the arguments) up front in `_from_hypertable_check_arguments`, and give the contract's refusals a remedy for the caller they are raised through (from_hypertable: re-run with corrected arguments). `Closes #1268`; `Addresses #1232`. Acceptance: F16r-01's `repro.sh` and F16-01's `repro.sql` (timescale harness).

#1269 (Tier 3, F19-02, rebuilt by its verifier): `archive.configure` stores `p_endpoint` exactly as given and both signers append '/' || bucket to it, so an endpoint ending in '/' produces a `//bucket/key` path and MinIO answers HTTP 400 to every PUT: every export and every tick fails after the read (loud, no loss). Nothing documents the spelling and configure checks nothing about the endpoint (it does reject bad `p_part_bytes` and `p_fetch_rows`). Fix shape: canonicalise the endpoint at configure (strip the trailing slash; refuse one with a path or no scheme, naming it) so a later export lands at the key either way; the rebuilt acceptance passes whichever way the fix goes. Coordinate with G3 (#1260, the prefix's canonical form) only through the issue comments: you own the endpoint, G3 owns the prefix. Acceptance: F19-02's `repro.verified.sql` (archive harness).

#1270 (Tier 3, F1-06): when transmute resumes an earlier attempt it checks the claim's column (#628) and grid (#574) but not the text_time encoding (`p_tt_prefix`, `p_tt_width`, `p_tt_radix`, `p_tt_unit`, `p_tt_alphabet`, `p_tt_discard_bits`, `p_tt_epoch`), so a re-run with another encoding takes over the claim, skips phase 1 because the old encoding's `pgpm_monolith_bound` CHECK already exists, and dies raw in the cutover's ATTACH after scanning the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, the bound and claim already committed. Fix shape: the resume compares every recorded encoding argument with the call's and refuses a mismatch up front with the remedy (transmute_abort, then re-run), the way the column and grid checks do. Acceptance: F1-06's `repro.sql`.

#1271 (Tier 3, F3-05): `_regrain_capture_names` looks the recorded capture function's oid up only within the delta's current schema (`p.pronamespace = nsp`), so once the delta has been moved with `SET SCHEMA`, `untransmute` drops the delta and leaves the SECURITY DEFINER capture function behind (and `uninstall.sql` uses the same helper), against the reference and the guide ("the delta and the function are found by oid, so one you renamed or moved since is still found"). Fix shape: resolve the function by its recorded oid wherever it lives, at every caller of the helper. Acceptance: F3-05's `repro.sql`.

#1272 (Tier 4, F4-02): the remedy `retain_disown` logs (the install's `_disown_unvouched_retirements`, method text at pgpm_core/install.sql ~3573) and docs/reference.md's retire entry repeat says only "drop the table by hand"; doing that leaves the attached `pgpm.part` row pointing at a dropped oid, after which every `retire()`/`retain()` logs `fail_retain_identity` for the range, `status().retain_drop_failures` climbs and the row takes a `retain_batch` slot every tick (the refusal is by design, #1038). Fix shape: the remedy names the whole repair (drop the table AND `pgpm.forget_missing()` or delete the row, or attach it back), in the log row's method, in `_disown_retirement`'s message and in the reference; a test that types the documented remedy and shows retention runs clean after it. Acceptance: F4-02's `repro.sql`.

#1273 (Tier 4, F18-02, rebuilt by its verifier): `_transmute_refuse_staging_squatter` hard-codes the remedy `drop table <nsp>.<rel>_pgpm_new` whatever kind of relation holds the staging name; against a sequence or a view the statement fails 42809 "is not a table" (the monolith and orphan-child refusals beside it use `_relkind_noun` or name no statement). Fix shape: the remedy names the right statement for the relkind (the `_relkind_noun` shape: drop sequence, drop view, ...), or names none; the rebuilt acceptance tests the statement named, not a spelling. Acceptance: F18-02's `repro.verified.sql`.

part_of: Addresses #1216 (the pg_inherits exemption that lets a partition of another table at a forward cell's name through)
what: #1274 (Tier 4, F1-05): `_transmute_refuse_child_holders` checks names with `_is_fine_child_label(kind, ...)`, which accepts ANY time label of the kind, so a monthly grid is refused by an operator's standalone table `sales_p2023` (a yearly label the grid could never mint, and set_regrain refuses coarser targets), and the message calls it a regrain orphan and tells the operator to `drop table` it, which would delete their rows; the reference and the code's comment limit the refusal to names pgpm could give this table's fine children. #1216 (open, Tier 3, re-found as F18-05): the same function's `not exists (select 1 from pg_inherits ...)` clause excuses any relation with a pg_inherits parent, so a partition of ANOTHER table holding a forward cell's name is not refused, the cell is left a hole (logged `fail_obtain_name`) and writes into it are refused. Fix shape: the label test is "a label this grid can produce" (the registered step and anchor, the regrain targets the step allows), and the exemption is "a partition of THIS parent", not any parent; one message that names the holder and a remedy that does not drop the operator's data. `Closes #1274`; `Addresses #1216` (say which bullets). Acceptance: F1-05's `repro.sql` and F18-05's `repro.sql` (the latter passes only if the hole is refused up front, not merely logged).

#1275 (Tier 4, F1-07): docs/reference.md lines 90-93 say a naive `timestamp` column holding wall time east of UTC runs on an hourly grid when `obtain` exceeds the offset, but transmute's frontier refusal (`_frontier_skew_limit` = now() + step + 1 h) refuses such a table's current rows (nine hours ahead for Tokyo) unless `p_force_frontier` is passed, which the paragraph never says. #1277 (Tier 4, F17-07 and F12r-01): CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section carries merge residue: a stale second tail of the #1161 bullet (lines ~523-530) saying `set_regrain` refuses an over-budget run, where it warns and stores the target, and five bullets that appear twice word for word (tests/93, tests/74, tests/141, untransmute with a pending detach, the outgoing-FK regrain restart). Fix shape: the reference paragraph states the frontier rule and `p_force_frontier` (or the paragraph is corrected to what works), with a doc guard in the shape of `bench/doc_transmute_no_default.sh` that types the paragraph's scenario; the CHANGELOG's stale tail removed and the duplicates folded, with a lint or guard that refuses a duplicated Unreleased bullet (the `check_living_docs.sh` shape) so the residue cannot return. `Closes #1275`, `Closes #1277`. Acceptance: F1-07's `repro.sql`, F17-07's `repro.sh`, F12r-01's `repro.sh`.

#1276 (Tier 4, F2-03): `_time_unit_breach` flags a `date` anchor off 00:00 UTC even for a whole-month step, whose bounds `_grid_floor` builds from `date_trunc('month', anchor)` so every bound lands at midnight and pgpm.part matches the catalog; the upgrade's `warn_grid_off_unit`, the matching row in docs/reference.md and `set_regrain`'s refusal all say the bounds disagree, which is false, and send the operator to a reconversion (and `set_regrain` refuses a 1-month target on a 3-month grid for that reason). Fix shape: the rule asks whether the REGISTERED step's bounds depend on the anchor's time part (a whole-month step does not), so a month grid with a noon anchor is neither flagged nor refused, while a day or hour grid still is; the reference row corrected. Acceptance: F2-03's `repro.sh`.

part_of: Addresses #1236 (bullets B08-01 and B08-02: a block comment before the assignment; an E'' backslash escape)
what: #1278 (Tier 5, F8-01, F12-06 rebuilt, F8-08): `scripts/check_quoted_splices.py` never reads a FOR ... IN SELECT loop's target as an assignment (an unmarked text local holding `quote_ident` output through a FOR form passes, the SELECT INTO twin is refused), and `bodies()` splits each file on the bare `$$` only, so a function body dollar-quoted with any other tag (`$fn$`) is never read at all. #1236 (open, Tier 5; bullets B08-01 and B08-02 re-found as F12-03 and F12-05): `strip_noise()` blanks `--` comments but not `/* */` block comments (a `/* */` before the `:=` hides the assignment) and has no handling for E'' backslash escapes (`E'it\'s'` closes the string early and blanks the unmarked assignment after it). Fix shape: read every dollar-quoted body whatever its tag, read a FOR loop target (and EXECUTE ... INTO) as an assignment, and lex block comments and E'' escapes correctly, with a `--selftest` case per shape (#1097 item 10). This PR adds or tightens a REPO-WIDE RULE: it is landed FIRST in its batch (`rule` in landq.txt) and you re-run the lint on the rebased head before it is enqueued; expect it to refuse spellings other PRs of this phase add. `Closes #1278`; `Addresses #1236 (bullets B08-01 and B08-02)`. Acceptance: F8-01's `repro.sh`, F12-06's `repro.verified.sh`, F8-08's `repro.sh`, F12-03's `repro.sh`, F12-05's `repro.sh`.

#1279 (Tier 5, F8-02 and F12r-07): `scripts/check_archive_object_keys.py` does not count a prefix reference bound as an `EXECUTE ... USING` argument as assembling a key, reads a call after FROM as a table name (so `unnest(array[cfg.prefix]) as u(p)` and `(values (cfg.prefix)) as u(p)` rename the prefix past it), and never follows `$n` parameters (a helper's `select $1 || $2` handed the prefix by position passes), against its docstring ("follows that value rather than a spelling of it"; a call's argument counts). Fix shape: follow the value through USING binds, FROM-item renames and positional parameters (or refuse any key assembly that reads the config row other than through `_owned_key`), with a `--selftest` case per shape. REPO-WIDE RULE: lands first in its batch (`rule`), re-run on the rebased head. Acceptance: F8-02's `repro.sh`, F12r-07's `repro.sh`.

part_of: Addresses #1180 (the three spellings F12r-06 added: to_jsonb(c) ->> 'relname', pg_identify_object(...).identity, an INTERSECT against the name)
what: #1287 (Tier 5, F12r-08): `scripts/check_archive_child_by_oid.py`'s rule 1 refuses a run-time name cast to regclass only when spelled `)::regclass`; `(...)::pg_catalog.regclass`, `CAST(... AS regclass)` and `regclass(...)` pass, though the docstring names the CAST and call forms. #1180 (open, Tier 5, the lint-limits issue: seven spellings documented so far, the standing default is "a lint beaten by a new spelling is not chased past one round: document the limit"; re-found as F12r-06 with three more: `to_jsonb(c) ->> 'relname'`, `pg_identify_object(...).identity`, an INTERSECT against the name). Fix shape: the cast rule reads every cast form the grammar allows (`::`, `CAST`, the function call, schema-qualified), with a `--selftest` case each; for the #1180 spellings, add what one round of lexing can read and DOCUMENT the rest as the lint's stated limit on #1180 (tests/archive/db/49 is the net), as the standing default says. `Closes #1287`; `Addresses #1180`. REPO-WIDE RULE: lands first in its batch (`rule`), re-run on the rebased head. Acceptance: F12r-08's `repro.sh`, F12r-06's `repro.sh` (as far as the fix reads).

#1280 (Tier 5, F11-02): `bench/ci_runs_lint_jobs.sh`'s check 5 accepts test.sh's `ci` on the spelling of a `"$0" lint` command and never requires that `ci` FAILS when the lint track fails, so a test.sh whose ci runs the lint and drops its failure (the #1183 symptom, PASS over a red Lint summary) passes the guard. Fix shape: the guard drives test.sh's ci logic against a stub whose lint fails and requires the FAIL verdict (behaviour, not spelling), with a mutation that drops the propagation. Acceptance: F11-02's `repro.sh`.

#1281 (Tier 5, F8-03): `bench/run_fh.sh:287` (driven by `run_rung_fh.sh`) calls `from_hypertable_cutover(..., p_regrain_batch => ...)`, a parameter the procedure does not have (it is `p_drain_batch`; the #291 rename sweep rewrote it), so every documented hypertable benchmark run dies "procedure ... does not exist" right after its copy; a never-read unit until this pass. #1282 (Tier 5, F8-05, rebuilt): `bench/run.sh`'s section-4f conservation gate judges "every history row still present" by `count(*)` before against `count(*) where id < MONO_HI` after, so a swap that loses row 5 and gains row 50 reads CONSERVED. Fix shape: the call uses the procedure's real parameter (and a static check, the `check_living_docs` shape, that every `pgpm.` call in bench/run*.sh names parameters the procedure declares); the gate compares the history rows by identity (ids, or a digest of the rows), the rebuilt acceptance runs the gate's own block. `Closes #1281`, `Closes #1282`. Acceptance: F8-03's `repro.sh`, F8-05's `repro.verified.sh`.

#1283 (Tier 5, F10-02 and F10-03): tests/timescale/db/65 (line ~128) and 66 (line ~136, a check labelled LIVENESS) look for leftover `pgpm.scratch` records by casting the table names to regclass AFTER the cutover, which yields the new partitioned tables' oids, while the records are keyed by the dropped hypertables' oids; a cutover whose `delete from pgpm.scratch where parent_oid = p_hypertable::oid` is removed leaves 6 and 3 rows and both files stay green. Fix shape: capture the hypertable's oid before the cutover and check the records by it (and grep the other timescale tests for the same pattern); the mutations through the wrappers that judge these files (`bench/hypertable_cutover_delta_by_record.sh`, `bench/hypertable_column_unit_rules.sh`, or `bench/tests_fail_on_defect.sh` if it dispatches timescale files: G27 owns that dispatch this phase, append under its block). `Closes #1283`. Acceptance: F10-02's `repro.sh`, F10-03's `repro.sh` (timescale harness).

#1284 (Tier 5, F16-02, F16-03, F16-04): tests/archive/db/16 Part B judges the Parquet object at the [-10000, 0) key by size (a strategy that archives 500 of 1000 rows passes 23/23), tests/archive/db/08 reads its NDJSON objects back by line count only (every line `"id":1` passes 22/22) and never reads its two 5-row chunks, and tests/archive/db/44 checks its two Parquet tick objects by the PAR1 prefix (a 4-byte object passes 15/15), each against its own header's identity promise. Fix shape: read each object back by identity with the chunk's rows (08 Part B's `parquet_object_holds` and the NDJSON line-id check are the shapes), with mutations through the wrappers that judge these files (`bench/archive_fn_s3_readback.sh` and siblings, or `bench/tests_fail_on_defect.sh` if it dispatches archive files: G27 owns that dispatch, append under its block). `Closes #1284`. Acceptance: F16-02's, F16-03's and F16-04's `repro.sh` (archive harness).

#1285 (Tier 5, F15-01): tests/72's only row-level-security assertion asks the role the policy names (t72_reader, a count of 400 over a symmetric 5-tenant fixture) and never a role it does not name, so an install whose transmute recreates `tenant_iso` TO PUBLIC passes all 15 assertions (and tests 159, 176, 185, 205, 218, 220, 241 and 250 too; the verifier checked). #1286 (Tier 5, F14-03): tests/27 asserts "all rows are preserved" after untransmute as `count(*) = 100` over a fixture whose rows are named (b1..b100). Fix shape: tests/72 asks a role the policy does NOT name and expects nothing, with an asymmetric fixture; tests/27 names the rows. YOU OWN `bench/tests_fail_on_defect.sh`'s dispatch this phase: add both files' injections there (G25 and G26 may append beneath your block for their timescale and archive files, and land after you); mutations in the catalogue's tests style (`MUTATION_SRC` = the test file). `Closes #1285`, `Closes #1286`. Acceptance: F15-01's `repro.sh`, F14-03's `repro.sh`.

#1288 (Tier 5, F12r-02): `stop_check.py` judges precision >= 0.7, fell rate <= 0.3 and coverage >= 0.9 on the two-decimal figures `pass_metrics.py` writes into the record, so 16/23 (0.696), 7/23 (0.304) and 26/29 (0.897) read as met and two such passes come back "stop: converged". #1289 (Tier 5, F12r-03): `pass_metrics.py` counts a candidate with no verdict, or an unknown verdict string ('known-open'), as FELL, inflating the fell rate the stopping criteria and the abandon-at-0.5 rule read, where the README says an unverified candidate is reported as such and is not a finding. #1290 (Tier 5, F12r-04): `decisions_queue.py`'s parse() skips any line not starting with `- D` instead of refusing it, so an indented, `*`-bulleted or lower-case BLOCKING entry is never read, `pending` exits 0 and `stop_check.py` lets the loop continue, against scripts/review/README.md ("the scripts refuse a line that does not have this shape"). Fix shape: write the exact fractions into the record (or judge from the counts) and have stop_check compare on them; count an unverified or unknown verdict as its own class and refuse an unknown string; refuse a malformed queue line; a `--selftest` case for each, which the lint workflow runs. These are scripts, not install files: no per-PR verification, but the self-tests are your acceptance beside the reproductions. `Closes #1288`, `Closes #1289`, `Closes #1290`. Acceptance: F12r-02's, F12r-03's and F12r-04's `repro.sh`.

part_of: Addresses #769 (bullet 2: the -infinity oldest value of a time or date control column reaches _grid_floor unchecked)
what: #769 bullet 2 (Tier 3, re-found as F13-02, its first reproduction): in `_transmute` only the newest value gets the infinity refusal (pgpm_core/install.sql ~10559) and the #895 non-finite check on the oldest value applies to `id` controls only, so a `time` or `date` control whose oldest value is `-infinity` stops with a raw `_grid_floor` error ("cannot convert infinity") instead of pgpm's refusal and remedy; nothing is committed either way. Fix shape: the non-finite refusal on the oldest value for every kind, before `_grid_floor`, with the remedy the +infinity side gives. `Addresses #769 (bullet 2)`; do not touch the issue's other bullets. Acceptance: F13-02's `repro.sql` (on the issue's pass-12 comment and in the pass-12 claim directory F13/F13-02).

part_of: Addresses #814 (the archive bullet: a direct strategy call's range read, empty-range check and recorded-chunk check parse p_lo under the session DateStyle while _object_stem parses it under its pinned one)
what: #814 (open since pass 6, the archive bullet at pgpm_archive/install.sql ~2445, re-found as F19-03, its first reproduction): in one direct strategy call the range read, the empty-range check and the recorded-chunk check parse `p_lo`/`p_hi` under the SESSION DateStyle while `archive._object_stem` parses them under its pinned 'ISO, MDY', so from a 'SQL, DMY' session the 2 January rows are archived under the 1 February chunk's key (the ledger row and the object disagree about which rows the key holds). Fix shape: every read of a bound text in the module goes through one pinned parse (the `_object_stem` shape, `set datestyle` on the function or an explicit canonical cast), and a test that drives the direct call from a 'SQL, DMY' session; grep the module for every `::timestamptz` of a bound. `Addresses #814` (the archive bullet; say which of the issue's sites the change covers). Acceptance: F19-03's `repro.sql` (archive harness; on the issue's pass-12 comment and in the claim directory F19/F19-03).
